# Files

Opening, reading, writing and flushing files through handles.

<h2 id="generic-read"><code>GENERIC_READ</code></h2>

```rux
pub const GENERIC_READ: uint32 = 0x80000000;
```

`GENERIC_READ`: the handle may read.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L14)

<h2 id="generic-write"><code>GENERIC_WRITE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const GENERIC_WRITE: uint32 = 0x40000000;
```

`GENERIC_WRITE`: the handle may write.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L19)

<h2 id="file-append-data"><code>FILE_APPEND_DATA</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_APPEND_DATA: uint32 = 0x00000004;
```

`FILE_APPEND_DATA`: the handle may append, and only append.
The access right that makes an append-only handle: every write lands at the end whatever the file pointer
says, which [`GENERIC_WRITE`](/docs/api/windows/files#generic-write) does not promise.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L26)

<h2 id="file-share-read"><code>FILE_SHARE_READ</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_SHARE_READ: uint32 = 0x00000001;
```

`FILE_SHARE_READ`: other openers may read while this handle is open.
Windows denies sharing by default, which is the opposite of every Unix. A file opened without this cannot be
opened for reading by anything else, including the same process.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L33)

<h2 id="file-share-write"><code>FILE_SHARE_WRITE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_SHARE_WRITE: uint32 = 0x00000002;
```

`FILE_SHARE_WRITE`: other openers may write while this handle is open.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L38)

<h2 id="file-share-delete"><code>FILE_SHARE_DELETE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_SHARE_DELETE: uint32 = 0x00000004;
```

`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`: the file may be renamed or deleted while this handle is open.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L43)

<h2 id="file-attribute-normal"><code>FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL: uint32 = 0x00000080;
```

`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL`: no attributes beyond being an ordinary file.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L48)

<h2 id="file-flag-backup-semantics"><code>FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS: uint32 = 0x02000000;
```

`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`: let [`CreateFileW`](/docs/api/windows/files#create-file-w) open a directory.
Without it a directory cannot be opened at all, which makes this the flag every metadata query needs.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L76)

<h2 id="file-flag-open-reparse-point"><code>FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT: uint32 = 0x00200000;
```

`FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`: open the symbolic link itself rather than what it points at.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L81)

<h2 id="file-flag-delete-on-close"><code>FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE: uint32 = 0x04000000;
```

`FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE`: remove the file when its last handle closes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L86)

<h2 id="file-flag-write-through"><code>FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH: uint32 = 0x80000000;
```

`FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH`: writes reach the device before the call returns.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L91)

<h2 id="create-file-w"><code>CreateFileW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func CreateFileW(fileName: *char16, desiredAccess: uint32, shareMode: uint32, securityAttributes: *var opaque, creationDisposition: uint32, flagsAndAttributes: uint32, templateFile: *var opaque) -> *var opaque
pub extern func CreateFileW(fileName: *char16, desiredAccess: uint32, shareMode: uint32, securityAttributes: *opaque, creationDisposition: uint32, flagsAndAttributes: uint32, templateFile: *opaque) -> *opaque
```

Creates or opens a file or device, taking a UTF-16 path.
Returns InvalidHandleValue on failure, not null. The share mode is not a default: passing zero denies every
other opener, which is Windows' behaviour and not most callers' intent.

| Overload                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Summary                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub extern func CreateFileW(fileName: *char16, desiredAccess: uint32, shareMode: uint32, securityAttributes: *var opaque, creationDisposition: uint32, flagsAndAttributes: uint32, templateFile: *var opaque) -> *var opaque` | Creates or opens a file or device, taking a UTF-16 path. |
| `pub extern func CreateFileW(fileName: *char16, desiredAccess: uint32, shareMode: uint32, securityAttributes: *opaque, creationDisposition: uint32, flagsAndAttributes: uint32, templateFile: *opaque) -> *opaque`             | Creates or opens a file or I/O device.                   |

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L134)

**Parameters**

| Name                  | Type                      | Description                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fileName`            | `*char16`                 | the path, as a null-terminated string                                                    |
| `desiredAccess`       | `uint32`                  | the access rights wanted, such as [`GENERIC_READ`](/docs/api/windows/files#generic-read) |
| `shareMode`           | `uint32`                  | what other openers may do meanwhile; zero denies them everything                         |
| `securityAttributes`  | `*var opaque` / `*opaque` | a security descriptor, or null for the default                                           |
| `creationDisposition` | `uint32`                  | one of the [`CreationDisposition`](/docs/api/windows/creation-disposition) values        |
| `flagsAndAttributes`  | `uint32`                  | the file attributes and flags                                                            |
| `templateFile`        | `*var opaque` / `*opaque` | a template whose attributes to copy, or null                                             |

**Returns**: the new handle, or [`InvalidHandleValue`](/docs/api/windows/types#invalid-handle-value) — which is not null

<h2 id="get-file-information-by-handle"><code>GetFileInformationByHandle</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetFileInformationByHandle(file: *var opaque, fileInformation: *var opaque) -> int32
```

Fills a BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION record for an open handle.
The record is 52 bytes: attributes at offset 0 (4 bytes), the creation, last-access and last-write
FILETIMEs at 4, 12 and 20 (8 bytes each), the volume serial number at 28, the size's high and low halves
at 32 and 36, the link count at 40, and the file index's halves at 44 and 48.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfileinformationbyhandle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfileinformationbyhandle)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L185)

**Parameters**

| Name              | Type          | Description                            |
| ----------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `file`            | `*var opaque` | an open file handle                    |
| `fileInformation` | `*var opaque` | receives the file's information record |

**Returns**: non-zero on success

<h2 id="set-file-time"><code>SetFileTime</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func SetFileTime(file: *var opaque, creationTime: *FileTime, lastAccessTime: *FileTime, lastWriteTime: *FileTime) -> int32
```

Sets the creation, last-access and last-write times of an open handle.
Each pointer may be null to leave that time alone.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-setfiletime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-setfiletime)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L196)

**Parameters**

| Name             | Type          | Description                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `file`           | `*var opaque` | an open file handle                           |
| `creationTime`   | `*FileTime`   | the creation time to set, or null to leave it |
| `lastAccessTime` | `*FileTime`   | the access time to set, or null to leave it   |
| `lastWriteTime`  | `*FileTime`   | the write time to set, or null to leave it    |

**Returns**: non-zero on success

<h2 id="get-final-path-name-by-handle-w"><code>GetFinalPathNameByHandleW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(file: *var opaque, filePath: *var char16, filePathLength: uint32, flags: uint32) -> uint32
```

Writes the final, resolved path of an open handle: symbolic links followed, short names expanded, case as
the filesystem stores it.
Returns the length written, without the terminator, or the required length when the buffer is too small,
or zero on failure. VOLUME_NAME_DOS (0) spells the answer with a drive letter where the file has one.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfinalpathnamebyhandlew](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfinalpathnamebyhandlew)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L210)

**Parameters**

| Name             | Type          | Description                              |
| ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `file`           | `*var opaque` | an open file handle                      |
| `filePath`       | `*var char16` | receives the resolved path               |
| `filePathLength` | `uint32`      | how many units `filePath` holds          |
| `flags`          | `uint32`      | the call's flag bits, combined with `\|` |

**Returns**: the length written, or zero on failure

<h2 id="flush-file-buffers"><code>FlushFileBuffers</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func FlushFileBuffers(file: *var opaque) -> int32
```

Flushes a file handle's writes to the device.
Returns zero on failure. This is what makes a write durable; FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH is the alternative that
does it on every write instead.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-flushfilebuffers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-flushfilebuffers)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/File.rux#L306)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type          | Description         |
| ------ | ------------- | ------------------- |
| `file` | `*var opaque` | an open file handle |

**Returns**: non-zero on success
